facts.fact: The Civil Status (Amendment) Act 2021, assented to on 4 November 2021 and commencing on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice, makes it the duty of the Chief Officer of Civil Status to maintain the registers of births, stillbirths and deaths, and has a death declared at a civil status office; the Act does not say the registers in use are kept digitally.
facts.system: register of births; Register of Deaths Occurring in Seychelles

systems.system: register of births; Register of Deaths Occurring in Seychelles
systems.country_label: registers maintained by the Chief Officer of Civil Status under section 15
systems.owner: Chief Officer of Civil Status, under the Minister responsible for civil status
systems.tiers: Chief Officer and civil status officers; deaths declared at a civil status office; medium of the register in use not stated

systems.country_label: registers not in use reproduced into digital format
systems.tiers: all registers not in use; access for persons the Minister authorises

systems.system: Notification of birth and notification of death (sections 32 and 81)
systems.country_label: notification of birth; notification of death
systems.owner: medical practitioners, nurses and midwives, to the Chief Officer and the Principal Secretary for health
systems.tiers: attending practitioner notifies within 3 days of a birth and 24 hours of a death; form or manner prescribed by the Minister for health; no electronic channel stated

systems.country_label: forms in electronic format; submission through an electronic medium
systems.tiers: permissive: the Chief Officer may provide forms electronically and may determine that statements, applications and signatures are submitted electronically

note: The Act is enabling law: the one fact is the owner. Section 18A (digitising disused registers) is archive, the notifications are notification, and sections 22A and 107A permit electronic forms and submissions without stating how the office makes the record, so they are left unclassified. Class of the registers themselves rests on the Act naming them the civil registrar's registers, not on any statement that they are digital: the parent may prefer to drop the fact.
